question.text: The Black-76 model is used for pricing:

answer.text: Options on Futures - a variant of Black-Scholes where the underlying is a futures contract

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, Black-76 is a variant of Black-Scholes used to calculate the theoretical price of Options on Futures, where the futures contract is the underlying. The original Black-Scholes formula uses spot price; Black-76 replaces it with the futures price. The Trap: The Series XVI workbook applies Black-76 to Options on Futures, while Options on Goods are valued using the original spot-underlying Black-Scholes formula - so "Options on Goods only" is wrong as the use case. Note: Because e^(-rT) x F = S, on the expiry day both Black-Scholes and Black-76 produce the same theoretical option price; the divergence appears only while time remains to expiry.
